Features.title: Bookmarks that organize themselves
Features.description: WakeMark syncs your X bookmarks, tags them by topic, sorts them into lists, and turns them into digests that arrive on your schedule. No setup, no manual sorting.

items.question: How do you access my bookmarks? Do I have to give you my X/Twitter password?
items.answer: Never. You connect via X/Twitter's official OAuth flow, which grants read-only access to your bookmarks. We never see your password, and you can revoke access from your X/Twitter settings at any time.

items.question: What happens to my data if I cancel?
items.answer: Your bookmarks and lists stay yours. If you cancel, you keep everything you've already synced. Resubscribe anytime to pick up where you left off.

items.question: How is this different from saving tweets to Notion or Readwise?
items.answer: Those tools store links. WakeMark actually reads, categorizes, and summarizes your bookmarks for you. You get auto-tagging by topic, shareable themed lists, and a digest that surfaces what matters instead of another pile of unread saves.

items.question: What does the AI auto-tagging actually do?
items.answer: When your bookmarks sync, our AI reads each one and assigns topic tags like "startup fundraising" or "CSS layout" or "machine learning." You don't configure anything. Tags appear automatically, and you can use them to filter, search, or build lists.

items.question: Is there a free trial?
items.answer: Yes. Every account starts with a 7-day free trial. After that, pricing starts at $59/year depending on when you join. Your price locks in for as long as you stay subscribed. Cancel anytime.

items.question: How often do bookmarks sync?
items.answer: Bookmarks sync automatically every day, plus you can trigger a manual sync whenever you want. There's no bookmark limit.

items.question: What does the email digest look like?
items.answer: It's a clean summary of your recent bookmarks, grouped by topic. Each entry includes the key takeaway in a sentence or two, plus a direct link to the original tweet. Think of it as a personal briefing, not a wall of links.

items.question: Is there a risk X/Twitter will block this or change their API?
items.answer: We use X/Twitter's official API within their published rate limits. If X/Twitter changes something on their end, we adapt. Your bookmarks already synced to WakeMark stay safe regardless of what happens with the API.
